content.text: A scalar discrete pole strictly inside the unit circle is asymptotically stable. Continuous-time linear systems are stable when the relevant closed-loop poles have negative real parts, under usual finite-dimensional LTI assumptions. A nonlinear local linearization can be useful near an operating point, but a plant may have multiple equilibria, regions of attraction, actuator limits and physical states that cannot be expressed by the linear model. Lyapunov-function methods can certify specific regions if assumptions and derivative conditions are established; the existence of a simulation trace with bounded states is not itself a Lyapunov proof. Domain context: 03_stability_equilibria_and_model_boundaries.md. A declared model is not a validated hardware controller.

Lyapunov-function methods can certify specific regions if assumptions and derivative conditions are established; the existence of a simulation trace with bounded states is not itself a Lyapunov proof.
